name: WhatWeb - Web Technology Fingerprinting
description: WhatWeb identifies web technologies: CMS (WordPress, Joomla, Drupal), frameworks, JavaScript libraries, web servers, analytics, and versions. Uses 1800+ plugins to fingerprint a target from headers, cookies, HTML, and behavior. First step to map a web app to known exploits and the right attack tooling.
notes:
=== BASIC SCAN ===
  whatweb <url>
  whatweb http://<ip>

=== AGGRESSION LEVELS ===
  whatweb -a 1 <url>   # stealthy (one request)
  whatweb -a 3 <url>   # aggressive (more plugins, more requests)
  whatweb -a 4 <url>   # heavy (all plugins)

=== SCAN MANY TARGETS ===
  whatweb -i live_hosts.txt
  whatweb <cidr>       # e.g. 10.10.10.0/24

=== VERBOSE + LOG ===
  whatweb -v <url>
  whatweb <url> --log-brief=whatweb.txt
  whatweb <url> --log-json=whatweb.json

=== TYPICAL USE ===
  # Identify CMS -> pick targeted tool:
  #   WordPress -> wpscan
  #   Joomla    -> joomscan
  #   Drupal    -> droopescan / drupalgeddon

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  wappalyzer (browser/CLI)
  nuclei -t technologies
  nmap --script http-*

examples.label: Scan a host list to JSON

recommended.note: Probe live hosts before fingerprinting them.
After identifying tech, scan for matching CVEs.
Identify the WAF in front of the app.

defense.why_it_works: Fingerprinting infers technologies from normal HTTP responses (headers, cookies, body markers). At low aggression it is a handful of ordinary requests, hard to distinguish from a real browser.
defense.impact: Maps the app to known-vulnerable components and the right exploit tooling.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1595.002] Default WhatWeb User-Agent; requests to fingerprinting paths (/wp-login.php, /administrator, favicon hashes); higher aggression causes bursts of plugin probe requests.
defense.artifacts: Web logs with WhatWeb UA; sequential requests to CMS-specific paths.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web http_user_agent="*WhatWeb*"
| stats count by src_ip, uri_path
defense.sentinel_kql:
_Im_WebSession
| where HttpUserAgentOriginal has "WhatWeb"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, Url, HttpUserAgentOriginal
defense.prevention: Suppress version banners (Server/X-Powered-By headers); generic error pages; WAF to flag scanner UAs; keep components patched so fingerprinting yields no easy wins.
